title: Best Restaurant Time Clock Software for Small Teams in 2026
summary: Missed clock-outs and Sunday-night payroll math? We compared restaurant time clock software on price, POS fit, and free-tier limits. See our top picks.
body_markdown:
It's 11 p.m. on a Sunday, and you're squinting at a smudged time card, trying to work out whether Sarah put in 6.5 hours on Tuesday or 8.5. Paper cards and shared spreadsheets break down fast in a restaurant, where one person might wait tables on Friday and cover the line on Saturday at a different wage rate. Add cash tips, split shifts, and a cook who forgets to clock out, and payroll turns into a reconstruction project.


Restaurant time clock software fixes the recording side of that problem. Staff clock in on a phone, a shared tablet, or the POS, and their hours land in timesheets. Whether breaks, overtime, role-based pay, and tips are handled automatically depends on the app and the plan. Choosing one is the harder part, because the options differ a lot on POS support, free-tier limits, and what the clock costs once you add a second location.


We compared six competitors on those points, and Homebase is covered separately in an unranked publisher note. Below you'll find our top picks, how we judged them, and where each one earns its spot and where it falls short.


## **The Short List: Best Restaurant Time Clock Software at a Glance**


- **7shifts:** the most restaurant-specific suite, with POS integrations and tip tools on higher tiers, though the clock runs in a separate app.
- **Sling:** free scheduling for up to 30 users, with a low per-user price for the time clock.
- **Clockify:** a low-cost kiosk with PIN and QR login, built for general use rather than restaurants.
- **Toast:** the natural pick if your restaurant already runs on Toast POS.
- **OnTheClock:** flat per-employee pricing, with payroll available as an add-on.
- **When I Work:** per-user scheduling with a separately priced time tracking option, for small hourly teams.

That gives us a stake in this topic, so here's how we handle it: Homebase isn't in the ranked list below, every app there was evaluated on its own merits, and we never accept payment or backlinks for a product mention.


For readers who want to see where we fit, we've reviewed Homebase on its own below, using the same template as the other apps.

## **How We Chose the Best Restaurant Time Clock Software**


We looked at time clock apps that restaurant owners can use for hourly front-of-house and back-of-house staff, and we evaluated each one against the same checklist:


- **Restaurant fit:** role-based wage rates, tip handling, and[break and overtime rules](https://www.joinhomebase.com/hr-compliance/labor-law-compliance) .
- **POS compatibility:** whether staff can clock in on the register or a shared tablet.
- **Clock-in options:** kiosk, phone, or POS.
- **Fraud controls:** PINs, photo capture, and geofencing.
- **Free-tier limits:** employee caps, location caps, and whether the clock itself is included.
- **Cost:** the monthly price at published rates, with the billing period noted.


We checked prices and free-tier limits against vendor pricing and help pages, read G2 and Capterra reviews, and quoted only reviews we could link to. This guide is based on vendor documentation and public reviews, not hands-on testing. It was reviewed by Christofer Peralta, who managed an independently owned fine dining restaurant in New York City and has more than 16 years in hospitality. Prices were last checked on October 10, 2026. Read our full[methodology](https://www.joinhomebase.com/methodology) .

## **Best Restaurant Time Clock Software**


### **7shifts**


7shifts is a restaurant scheduling platform that has grown into time tracking, tip tools, and payroll. It suits restaurants that want software built around front and back of house, with POS integrations to match. The catch is that clocking in runs through a separate 7punches app, and the time clock isn't on the free plan.


**Best for:** Restaurants that want restaurant-specific scheduling and POS ties alongside the clock.


**Rating:** G2 4.5 (123 reviews) · Capterra 4.7 (1,212 reviews). Sources:[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/7shifts/reviews) and[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/123038/7shifts-Restaurant-Scheduling/reviews/) .


**What it is:** A restaurant-specific scheduling and labor platform with a time clock, plus tip and payroll tools on higher tiers.


**Key features:**


- Clock-in on tablets and phones through the 7punches app.
- Availability, shift swaps, and time-off requests.
- Labor alerts for overtime, breaks, and clock-ins.
- POS integrations, including Toast, Square, and Clover.
- Optional 7shifts Payroll.


**Pricing:** The Comp plan is free for one location and up to 15 employees, without time clocking. Essentials is $39.99 per location per month billed annually ($44.99 monthly) for up to 30 employees and adds basic time clocking. Pro is $79.99 per location per month billed annually, or $89.99 billed monthly, with advanced time clocking and a higher employee limit. Premium is $134.99 per location per month billed annually, or $149.99 billed monthly, and includes tip management. 7shifts Payroll adds $6 per employee paid per month on top of the plan price. See[7shifts pricing](https://www.7shifts.com/pricing/) .


**What users like:** A Capterra reviewer said the built-in messaging, group chats, and announcements reduce "the need for multiple apps, phone calls, and texts."[Read the reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/123038/7shifts-Restaurant-Scheduling/reviews/) .


**What users criticize:** Capterra reviewers describe occasional slow loading, unexpected logouts, and server crashes that can get in the way of clocking in.[Read the reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/123038/7shifts-Restaurant-Scheduling/reviews/) .


**Our take:** If you want restaurant-specific scheduling with POS ties, this is the most tailored option here. If you want a single app for clocking in, plan on installing 7punches alongside it, and test it during the trial given the logout complaints. Toast users should also know that 7shifts' help center says Toast, not 7shifts, charges $50 per location per month for integration access, on top of your 7shifts plan.


### **Sling**


Sling is a scheduling app with a free plan for up to 30 users and a low per-user price for time tracking. It works for small restaurants that start with scheduling and add the clock later. Mobile time tracking starts on Premium and kiosk clock-in on Business, so the free tier won't replace a time clock.


**Best for:** Small restaurants that want free scheduling now and a cheap clock later.


**Rating:** G2 4.4 (88 reviews) · Capterra 4.6 (212 reviews). Sources:[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/sling/reviews) and[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/142542/Sling/reviews/) .


**What it is:** A scheduling and team messaging app with a paid time clock and labor tools.


**Key features:**


- Free scheduling, time-off requests, and messaging.
- Mobile time tracking on Premium.
- Kiosk time tracking on a shared tablet on Business.
- Labor-cost management and overtime tracking on paid plans.
- Toast POS sync for sales and shift data.


**Pricing:** Free for up to 30 users on standard accounts, without time tracking. Premium is $2 per user per month ($1.70 billed annually), and Business is $4 ($3.40 annually). Accounts created through Toast use separate packaging. See[Sling pricing](https://getsling.com/pricing/) .


**What users like:** A Capterra reviewer in May 2026 said "the swap shifts save literally hours of my life," and valued seeing availability in the mobile app.[Read the reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/142542/Sling/reviews/) .


**What users criticize:** Another May 2026 reviewer reported delayed notifications and calendar syncing that doesn't always work with Google Calendar.[Read the reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/142542/Sling/reviews/) .


**Our take:** Per-user pricing is cheap for a 10-person café and adds up on larger teams, where a flat per-location price can come out lower. The shared-tablet kiosk is on the pricier Business tier, which matters if your staff clock in at the line rather than on their phones.


### **Clockify**


Clockify is a general time tracker that offers a kiosk where staff clock in with a PIN or QR code. It fits owners who want a cheap, simple clock and will handle scheduling elsewhere. The free plan stops at five users, and nothing about it is built around restaurant tips or POS data.


**Best for:** Owners who want a low-cost kiosk and not much else.


**Rating:** G2 4.5 (203 reviews) · Capterra 4.8 (9,270 reviews). Sources:[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/clockify/reviews) and[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/169607/Clockify/reviews/) .


**What it is:** A time tracking app that turns any internet-connected device into a clock-in kiosk.


**Key features:**


- Kiosk on a tablet, computer, or phone.
- PIN and QR code login.
- iOS and Android apps.
- QuickBooks integration, plus an API and webhooks.
- Reports on hours, breaks, and time off.


**Pricing:** Free for up to five users. Kiosk-only limited seats cost $0.99 per month, or $0.79 billed annually, on the Basic plan, with higher tiers priced above that. Standard full-user plans are priced separately. See[Clockify pricing](https://clockify.me/pricing) .


**What users like:** A G2 reviewer in September 2026 said the interface is "very intuitive," which helped the team adapt.[Read the reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/clockify/reviews) .


**What users criticize:** An August 2026 G2 reviewer reported that the web app sometimes stops working in Chrome and logs them out, occasionally blocking them from logging back in.[Read the reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/clockify/reviews) .


**Our take:** Setup is quick and the kiosk price is hard to beat. Clockify tracks billable rates for client work, which isn't the same as role-based pay, so check how you'd handle a server who also works the bar. These reviews describe general time tracking, not restaurant use.


### **Toast**


Toast is a restaurant POS with a built-in time clock. Staff enter a POS access code, pick a job, and clock in or out on the terminal, and breaks work the same way. It fits restaurants already on Toast, since hours, tips, and sales live in one system. Toast doesn't publish standalone time clock pricing.


**Best for:** Restaurants already on Toast POS.


**Rating:** G2 4.2 (371 reviews) · Capterra 4.1 (554 reviews). These are ratings for Toast POS overall, not the time clock alone. Sources:[G2](https://www.g2.com/sellers/toast) and[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/136301/Toast-POS/reviews/) .


**What it is:** A restaurant POS whose time clock and team tools connect to Toast Payroll.


**Key features:**


- Clock in, clock out, and take breaks on the POS terminal.
- Job selection at clock-in, so hours go to the right role.
- A unique POS access code for each employee.
- Schedule enforcement settings for early and late clock-ins.
- The free MyToast app, where staff can see their shifts, breaks, and tips.


**Pricing:** Toast doesn't publicly list standalone time clock or team management pricing. Toast advertises a POS and payroll bundle for eligible new, single-location restaurants at $69 per month plus $9 per employee, and its POS pricing starts at $69 per month, with custom pricing for larger setups. That bundle isn't the price of the time clock alone, so confirm current terms with Toast. See[Toast pricing](https://pos.toasttab.com/pricing) .


**What users like:** A Capterra reviewer in January 2026, a waitress, wrote "I love Toast. Easy to use, Efficient."[Read the reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/136301/Toast-POS/reviews/) .


**What users criticize:** A manager wrote on Capterra in April 2026 that support was lacking for back-end issues and that staff did not always seem knowledgeable.[Read the reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/136301/Toast-POS/reviews/) .


**Our take:** If you're on Toast, start here, since the clock, tips, and sales share a system. Toast's help documentation describes the clock as part of the POS, and employees need a profile and POS access code before they can use it. If you run a different POS, this likely isn't an option.


### **OnTheClock**


OnTheClock is a time and attendance app with desktop, mobile, web, and kiosk clock-ins plus GPS and geofencing. It prices per employee, which keeps the bill predictable for a small team. Payroll is available as an add-on. It also publishes its own restaurant time clock roundup that ranks itself first.


**Best for:** Small teams that want flat, predictable pricing.


**Rating:** G2 4.4 (282 reviews) · Capterra 4.7 (806 reviews). Sources:[G2](https://www.g2.com/sellers/ontheclock) and[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/130009/OnTheClock-com/reviews/) .


**What it is:** A time and attendance app with scheduling, PTO tracking, and an optional payroll add-on.


**Key features:**


- Clock-in by desktop, mobile, web, or kiosk.
- GPS, geofencing, and IP restrictions.
- Overtime calculations.
- Scheduling and PTO management.
- Payroll integrations.


**Pricing:** Time tracking is $4 per employee per month plus a $5 monthly base fee. Integrated payroll adds $6 per employee per month plus a $40 monthly base fee and a one-time $250 onboarding fee. See[OnTheClock pricing](https://www.ontheclock.com/pricing) .


**What users like:** A Capterra reviewer in September 2026 called it "easy to use" and liked having hours and everything else in one spot.[Read the reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/130009/OnTheClock-com/reviews/) .


**What users criticize:** A September 2026 Capterra reviewer reported the app sometimes lagged, making clock-in difficult, so they had to check whether the punch registered. A second recent reviewer described missed punches and early clock-outs that needed manual fixes.[Read the reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/130009/OnTheClock-com/reviews/) .


**Our take:** It's strong on predictable pricing and general time tracking, though nothing here is restaurant-specific. The vendor ranks itself first in its own restaurant guide, so we took pricing and features from its pricing page rather than its blog. Test the mobile clock-in during the trial given the lag reports.


### **When I Work**


When I Work is a scheduling app for hourly teams with time tracking available as a separate pricing option. Plans start at $2.50 per user per month before time tracking is added, with no permanent free plan, only a 14-day trial. It isn't built for restaurants, but it suits small teams that want per-user pricing.


**Best for:** Small hourly teams that want per-user pricing and simple scheduling.


**Rating:** G2 4.4 (411 reviews) · Capterra 4.5 (1,300 reviews). Sources:[G2](https://www.g2.com/sellers/when-i-work) and[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/121248/When-I-Work/reviews/) .


**What it is:** A scheduling and team messaging app for shift-based businesses, with an optional time tracking and attendance add-on and payroll and POS integrations.


**Key features:**


- Auto scheduling and unlimited schedule templates.
- GPS clock-in controls with the optional time tracking and attendance add-on.
- Labor forecasting and standard labor reports.
- Time-off and availability management.
- Payroll and POS integrations.


**Pricing:** Essentials starts at $2.50 per user per month, Pro is $5, and Premium is $8, all before time tracking is added. When I Work shows Time Tracking & Attendance as a separate pricing option, so confirm the total for your plan before comparing it with tools that include clocking in their headline price. There's a 14-day free trial and no permanent free plan. See[When I Work pricing](https://wheniwork.com/pricing) .


**What users like:** A Capterra reviewer in April 2026 said it "makes scheduling simple" and keeps the team connected, and liked the mobile app.[Read the reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/121248/When-I-Work/reviews/) .


**What users criticize:** The same reviewer said notifications sometimes lag, reporting is limited, and the mobile app can feel slow.[Read the reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/121248/When-I-Work/reviews/) .


**Our take:** The low starting price is attractive for a small team, but per-user pricing climbs with headcount, and the time and attendance cost needs confirming before you budget. It's a fit for a café or small restaurant that mostly needs scheduling with a clock attached, and a weaker fit if you need tip pooling.


## **Frequently Asked Questions About Restaurant Time Clock Software**


### **Is there free time clock software for restaurants?**


Yes, but free plans usually cap employees or locations, or leave out the clock itself. 7shifts' free plan doesn't include time clocking, Sling's free plan covers scheduling only, and Clockify's free plan stops at five users. Check each vendor's live pricing page before you choose.


### **How long do I have to keep restaurant time cards?**


Under the Fair Labor Standards Act, covered employers generally must keep payroll records for at least three years and records used to calculate wages, including[time cards](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/time-card) and work schedules, for at least two years. The[U.S. Department of Labor](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/21-flsa-recordkeeping) explains this in Fact Sheet #21. State laws may require longer, so check your[state's labor rules](https://www.joinhomebase.com/state-labor-laws) .


### **Can restaurant employees clock in on the POS?**


Some can. Toast runs its time clock on the POS terminal, while 7shifts uses a separate 7punches app and connects to several POS systems. Other apps use a shared tablet or staff phones. List your POS before you shop, and confirm the vendor's integrations page names it.


### **How do you stop buddy punching in a restaurant?**


Look for individual PINs, photo capture at clock-in, and GPS or geofencing, which make it harder for one person to clock in for another. Early clock-in limits help too, along with manager approvals and an audit trail that shows who edited a punch and when. Features vary by plan, and our guide to[buddy punching](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/buddy-punching) covers the common tactics.


### **How do you track tips and multiple wage rates?**


Look for a clock that lets staff pick a role at clock-in, so each hour pays at the right rate, and that imports tips from your POS or lets staff declare[cash tips](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/tip-tracker) . Tip pooling often costs extra or sits on higher tiers.[Tip Manager](https://www.joinhomebase.com/tip-manager) is one example of a tip add-on.


### **What happens when someone forgets to clock out?**


It depends on the app. Look for reminders, automatic[clock-out](https://www.joinhomebase.com/glossary/clock-out) after a set time, or a way for employees to add a note that a manager can review and fix, with an audit trail of the edit. Overtime alerts catch the cost before payroll closes and help you avoid[payroll errors](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/payroll-errors) , and our guide to[time theft prevention](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/time-theft-prevention-for-teams) explains more.


## **Which Restaurant Time Clock Fits Your Setup**


If your restaurant already runs on Toast, look at Toast's integrated time clock first. If you're a small team on a tight budget, compare Sling's paid clock against Clockify's kiosk seats and five-user free plan. If you want restaurant-specific scheduling with POS ties, evaluate 7shifts after confirming which tier and add-ons you need.


For several locations, calculate costs using your actual number of locations and employees rather than comparing headline prices, since per-location and per-user pricing flip in your favor at different headcounts. Where a trial is available, test the clock through a full pay period. For Toast, request a demo and confirm the time clock, POS, and payroll setup with the vendor before committing. For a closer look at what that payroll costs you, our guide to[managing labor costs](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/how-to-manage-labor-costs) is a good next read.
